correctness.rationale: The kernel of a rank-two prefix equals the last factor's conic line. A new factor drops rank iff its perpendicular plane contains that line, and the only conic point orthogonal to an isotropic point is itself. The resulting row is isotropic by S(v)^2=vv^T. For rank one, right multiplication acts on its row by cross product up to sign. The result vanishes only for parallel vectors and otherwise has norm -(w·v)^2. When the old norm is a negative square the perpendicular binary form has determinant in the negative-square class and is split, giving two distinct conic choices; the isotropic row case gives just the annihilating choice and q nonisotropic results. These counts are valid over odd extension fields as well. The transient I,R block resolvent has summed first-row numerator 1+hz and the displayed determinant; the waiting time to enter I has mean q+1 and the two hitting-time equations give (q+1)(q+2)/2 more steps. In O(q) steps the expected number of visits to I is bounded by 1+2h times the number of steps, giving vanishing absorption probability. At q^2 scale the entrance wait divided by q^2 tends to zero; starting from I the survival weights have principal coefficient (a−lambda_minus)/(lambda_plus−lambda_minus) tending to one, and (1−lambda_plus)(1−lambda_minus)=2h^2 gives the stated exponent. The indexing starts at k=1 throughout.

value.rationale: For this natural three-dimensional nilpotent orbit, rank alone hides the mechanism of extinction. The exact row-class refinement gives a benchmark in which loss of rank and annihilation occur on genuinely different scales, and quantifies the constant 2 in the slow absorption limit. That is not a recomputation of single-matrix ranks or an arbitrary small-word slice.
residual_risks: No implication for arbitrary factor distributions, higher dimensions, or individual output fibers is established.
